a: Compilers translate whole programs ahead of time; interpreters execute source incrementally.
A lexer (tokenizer) splits source text into tokens.
A parser builds a syntax tree from tokens according to a grammar.
An AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) represents program structure without surface syntax details.
Bytecode is portable intermediate code executed by a VM (e.g. JVM, CPython).
JIT compiles hot code at runtime for speed while keeping portability.
Static typing checks types before run; dynamic typing checks mostly at runtime.
Type inference lets the compiler deduce types without explicit annotations.
Common GC: mark-sweep, generational, reference counting (with cycle caveats).
A linker combines object files and libraries into an executable.
